payload.reason: Findings addressed: BT1, BT4, BT5, STD2, STD3 (codex round 3, seq 15). Each was independently re-derived before acting; all five held. BT1 (S3-B8): dom.rs gains Document::references(), one extractor classifying every URL-bearing attribute as Fetch (src, srcset/imagesrcset per candidate, poster, data, background, longdesc, manifest, ping, xlink:href, href on link/use/image), Navigation (a/area href, action, formaction, cite, meta refresh url), or Base, and recursing into srcdoc documents with a srcdoc: context prefix. Both the same-origin step and the only-asset step consume it; the same-origin step additionally fails on any <base> (a rebase Codex did not name) and keeps the CSS scans of style attributes and elements. The only-asset step counts Fetch references only, so a second local image or a srcdoc-nested foreign image now fails. New default-harness test file tests/oracles.rs (12 tests) makes the adversarial cases durable and in-gate: both round-3 counterexamples, base rebase, ping, classification of 13 attribute forms, a conforming page yielding exactly its stylesheet, plus all prior CSS accept/reject probes and a markup-contract name-distinctness check. BT4 (S3-B6): El::field now panics on more than one match and on a hidden match; hidden means the hidden attribute, aria-hidden=true, inline display:none or visibility:hidden, or a head/template ancestor, on the element or any ancestor (walks rcdom parent links). Residual, recorded: hiding by stylesheet class rule is beyond a parsed DOM and is assigned to the Layer 2 Playwright proof at acceptance. BT5 (S3-B9): the malformed-Card-ID scenario now also asserts the Card-not-found error text and reuses the no-Card-identity-or-stream oracle. STD2 (C13): tokenization is an Iterator (Tokens::next) consumed one token at a time; no Vec<Token> is built. STD3 (C11): migrations_unchanged reads the after-state first and borrows the recorded before-state; Clone removed from AppliedMigration. Two of my own test expectations were wrong, not the oracles: html5ever hoists body attributes earlier in document order, and parses noscript content as raw text (field absent, which readers already reject). Gate: fmt, clippy -D warnings, ast-grep, cargo deny clean; unit 31 green, oracles 12 green (run separately since cargo test halts at the red behavior target), behavior 57 prior scenarios green, 62 S3 scenarios red on missing serve, 351 fixture steps green, 128 step definitions.
payload.summary: Behavior-tests review round 3 remediated: BT1 one browser-fetch extractor (srcset, srcdoc, base, ping, meta refresh) feeds both B8 proofs with durable adversarial tests; BT4 field lookup requires uniqueness and visibility; BT5 malformed-ID 404 proves no fabricated Card; STD2 iterator tokenizer; STD3 clone removed

payload.reason: Codex BT6 (seq 17): a script inside an srcdoc iframe passed every S3-B8 assertion, and its fix said not to extend the harness into a partial browser. Kendall had asked at the start of this stage whether Playwright, not Rust libraries, was the tool for these tests; the answer was yes and I failed to apply it, spending three rounds on a URL resolver, a CSS Syntax L3 tokenizer, a srcset/srcdoc walker, and a visibility model. This is the PER-83 mechanism-leak pattern: churn concentrated on simulating one mechanism. The limb is cut, not layered: deleted tests/behavior/console/css.rs, tests/oracles.rs, the reference extractor and hidden-walker in dom.rs (about 550 lines). Layer 1 B8 now proves only what markup shows: no script element, no on* attribute, no iframe/frame/frameset/object/embed/base/style element, no srcdoc/style/srcset/imagesrcset/ping attribute (new step: no response body contains an embedded document, a base element, or inline CSS), every href/src/action/formaction/poster/data same-origin via the url crate, exactly one asset (any src or link href) which is the stylesheet, served text/css, and the stylesheet text contains no url(, @import, or backslash (a policy on our own CSS, not a parser). Field lookup keeps uniqueness, drops hidden detection. Assigned to Layer 2 (Playwright, real browser, own just recipe, before acceptance): load-time fetch set is exactly the page and the stylesheet via a request listener; every envelope field toBeVisible; zero console errors. Gerkin B8 scenario comment names the split. Gate: fmt, clippy, ast-grep, deny clean; 57 prior scenarios green, 62 S3 red on missing serve, 351 fixture steps green, 129 step definitions.

Amendments, by step. Verified state after the R1 edit: the behavior test target compiles; the sink table now has separate DecisionSummary and StageSummary rows, the payload sink is gone from Stage and StageSummary, and the inspector equality step reads the history `payload` member by presence.

Step 5 (Reader open): the reader opens the database as a normal read-only live WAL reader: read-only connect options, journal_mode left unspecified, immutable false; WAL and SHM sidecars are expected. It never calls the writer's create/migrate/chmod open path and never falls back to a writing open on failure (R9). The no-background-task fence means no application workflow, projection or polling tasks; SQLx pool connection maintenance under the chosen pool settings is permitted (R8).

Step 7 (Listener/ConfigSource/Startup): add `impl std::fmt::Display for ConfigSource` per skeleton revision 6: Flag -> flag, Env -> env, DotEnv -> dotenv, Default -> default, written with `f.write_str`. Every other rendering of a source name goes through this impl. Add one unit test asserting the four spellings (R2). A small private RFC3339 formatting helper in this crate is acceptable; do not add a public helper (R5).

Step 8 (templates/view structs): `<time datetime="...">` attributes are populated only from typed server timestamps, formatted by the server, with the same value as visible text; producer-supplied text never enters an attribute (R3). Inspector view: the payload element is rendered only when the history entry carries a `payload` member; for a stage event without one, the inspector renders stage and summary as typed fields and no `data-role=payload` element at all. An Askama render failure produces a fixed plain-text 500 after buffering the render, so no partial HTML is ever written; storage and schema failures keep the HTML error page; no new error variant (R6).

Step 10 (handlers): the Card page takes its identity fields from the matching `QueueCard` in the same request's queue read; there is no second list query. A Card absent from that read is the existing missing-Card error page (R4).

Step 11 (cucumber flip): expected transition is 57 passed / 62 failed -> 119 passed / 0 failed. 117/119 is a failure to investigate, never an acceptance state.

Step 13 (browser flip): if the fetch-set test fails on a favicon request, escalate with the observed request in evidence; do not add an icon or relax the test preemptively (R7).

All other steps, fences, decisions and the definition of done at sequence 43 stand.
